title: add jsonschema strict-mode for response_format + OpenAI compatibility fixes
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: provide a robust, predictable structured-output API surface by adding a strict JSON Schema validation mode for the response_format parameter and harmonizing behavior with the OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR adds server-side validation of generated outputs against user-provided JSON Schemas, clearer validation error messages, and an opt-in strict mode that will cause requests to fail fast when outputs do not conform. The goal is to reduce downstream parsing/validation complexity for integrators and improve observable signals for quality regressions. Changes in this PR: 1) Add response_format.strict boolean (server-side) that enforces schema validation and returns structured error details when validation fails. 2) Implement SchemaValidator component with streaming-aware validation hooks so schema checks run incrementally during generation to avoid large memory blowups. 3) Add OpenAI-compat shims so response_format and function_call semantics map to the same validation lifecycle used by Redwood APIs. 4) Improve error messages: response now includes a concise validation_summary and a validation_errors array with path, expected, and actual summary. 5) Update streaming protocol to emit a validation status event at the end of stream and to provide early non-fatal warning events when partial validation mismatches are detected during streaming (configurable). 6) Add unit and integration tests (validator fuzz tests, streaming tests, OpenAI-compat examples) and docs for SDK usage and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Implement core validator and API flag - [x] Streaming-aware hooks and event protocol - [x] OpenAI compatibility mappings and backward-compat tests - [x] Add extensive unit + integration tests, including regression tests from SUP-7642 - [x] Update docs and CHANGELOG - [x] Run perf pass and add small optimizations for common schemas Backwards compatibility / migration notes: default behavior is unchanged (response_format without strict still validates non-fatally and returns best-effort output). opt-in behavior: clients can set response_format.strict=true (or the OpenAI-compatible parameter response_format_strict=true) to enable failure-on-invalid. When strict is enabled the server will return HTTP 400 with body containing validation_summary and validation_errors if the final output does not match schema. Streaming behavior: for strict=true the final validation result is emitted as a terminal validation event (and the stream is closed with a non-0 status for WebSocket). For clients using incremental parsing, the PR adds a WARN event type when partial tokens appear to violate the schema so clients can surface warnings earlier; these warnings do not cause the request to fail unless strict is set. Performance: validator runs incrementally and reuses compiled validators per model/schema key; a simple microbenchmark in the perf-suite shows <= 8% median token latency overhead for small schemas and <1% for noop validation path (cache hit). Security: we sandbox schema compilation and limit recursion/complexity to protect against DoS schemas. Linear/Jira: references ENG-4123, PM-88, SUP-7642. Polices: added a new config max_schema_nodes (defaults to 5000) to prevent pathological schemas. Docs: updated redwood-docs/api/response_format.md and added an example in openai-compat.md. Rollout: feature behind feature-flag jsonschema_strict; will be enabled for canary customers then ramped to GA after a week of telemetry.

review_comments: Marco Chen (2026-02-19): Nice work. Two questions: 1) how do we surface validation errors in the OpenAI-compatible response payload? We should include an `validation` object in the top-level choices[0].message.metadata for compatibility. 2) Any perf knobs for very large schemas?

Aisha Patel (2026-02-19): Replied: added a validation_summary field in the top-level payload and included a compatibility shim that injects validation metadata into choices[0] when openai_compat=true. For large schemas we added max_schema_nodes and compilation caching; documented in perf notes.
Lena Rodriguez (2026-02-20): Please add an integration test that simulates a streaming client disconnect mid-validation and ensure we don't leak compiled validators/pending futures.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-20): Added test_streaming_disconnect and updated the validator to cancel compilation futures on disconnect. Tests pass locally.
Samir Gupta (2026-02-21): Approval pending CI. Verify that WARN events are opt-in and cannot be confused with validation failures by clients parsing older SDKs.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-22): Updated protocol to include an explicit event_type field (WARN | VALIDATION_RESULT) and added SDK parsing examples.
merge_notes: Canary rollout enabled via feature-flag. Telemetry tracked under ENG-4123.
release_notes: Added opt-in response_format.strict (JSON Schema) that enforces strict validation of generated outputs. Streaming emits validation events; OpenAI compatibility mappings included. See response_format.md for migration guidance.
qa_notes: Tested with streaming and non-streaming clients; added fuzz harness for schema edge cases. Watch telemetry for validation_error_rate and token_latency_pct95 after rollout.
observability_changes: Added validation_error_count metric, validation_latency histogram, and an alert when validation_error_rate spikes > 1% over 5m. Dashboard updated at Observability > API > Validation.
docs_changes: Updated response_format.md and openai-compat.md with examples for strict=true and recommendations for handling WARN events. Added migration snippet for SDKs.
perf_impact_summary: Incremental validation adds up to 8% token latency in worst-case small-schema scenarios; typical overhead <2% due to caching. Benchmarks in perf/benchmarks/validators/README.md.
